history.summary: Modern Sai Baba temple at Chidambara Rao Street, Kothapeta, Kurnool, known locally as 'Dakshina Shirdi', near the banks of the Tungabhadra. A 2010 report on the Shirdi Sai Baba movement notes the Kurnool temple celebrates all festivals of the Shri Saibaba Sansthan Trust, Shirdi. No construction/founding date found in web sources. PROVISIONAL IDENTITY: several Sai Baba temples exist in Kurnool (Balaji Nagar Road, Court Road, Konda Reddy Buruju, etc.); this file documents the most prominent one (Chidambara Rao Street, Kothapeta) — verify it is the CSV's intended referent.

name: Shirdi Sai Baba Temple
town_description: Kurnool, on the banks of the Tungabhadra in western Andhra Pradesh, is one of the oldest cities of the region — a former capital of Andhra State (1953-1956). It is a pilgrimage hub ringed by major shrines: the Jagannatha Gattu hill temples, Mahanandi, Ahobilam, Srisailam and Mantralayam are all within reach, and the Kondareddy Buruju fort tower stands in the old town.
